versions.summary: Materialised in the repository. JSON is authoritative; statuses recomputed by scripts/security-verify.mjs. Scratchpad mutation records EV-MUT-{L2,L3,H2,L1,L4,L5} replaced by reproducible mutation evidence EV-KB-* (security/mutation/cases.json, 66 cases). EV-CRSF-SELFTEST and EV-PROBE-LOW-S added. Owner sign-off field added (PENDING). Framework lock bootstrapped. No control definition, release class or minimum level changed.

versions.summary: Evidence closure for release-blocking controls: 11 closed (CR-API-002, CR-TELEGRAM-001, CR-AUTH-001/002/003/007, CR-SESSION-002/003/005/007, CR-CONC-005); 6 new test files, 37 new mutation cases; the Phase 2A surviving cron mutation is now KILLED. No application code changed.

changes.why_sufficient: P1 cron: missing/wrong/same-length/malformed secrets rejected before any run, purge, delivery or alert; removing the check or comparing by length is killed. P2 webhook: Phase 2A case. P3: unconfigured CRON_SECRET and webhook secret fail closed; removing either guard is killed (E4 for every sub-property).
changes.remains_unproven: Vercel Cron and Telegram delivering the headers in production; constant-time comparison is not behaviourally observable.
changes.reason: new reproducible evidence (Phase 2B)

changes.why_sufficient: P1 secret bypass and length-only compare killed; P2 removing the private-chat guard killed by the existing "webhook ignores ..." tests (no database call); P3 redelivered update_id processed once, killed both when the claim is skipped and when 23505 is treated as new.
changes.remains_unproven: Primary-key uniqueness under truly concurrent deliveries (the fake models the primary key; Postgres enforces it).
changes.reason: new reproducible evidence (Phase 2B)

changes.why_sufficient: P1-P3 from Phase 2A cases; P4 issued-at and expiration-time must equal the stored challenge (two mutations SURVIVED until the new test - a real evidence gap, now closed), future issued-at and expired challenge killed; P5 address comparison removal killed.
changes.remains_unproven: Interop with real wallets; viem parseSiweMessage correctness itself.
changes.reason: new reproducible evidence (Phase 2B)

changes.why_sufficient: P1 Phase 2A; P2 consuming the challenge or issuing a session after a failed signature is killed by the existing login and H1 tests.
changes.reason: new reproducible evidence (Phase 2B)

changes.why_sufficient: P3 unpinned isValidSignature and ignored block-hash disagreement killed; P4 provider error as VALID, deadline as VALID and ignored getCode disagreement killed.
changes.remains_unproven: Behaviour against real mainnet providers and real Safe contracts.
changes.reason: new reproducible evidence (Phase 2B)

changes.why_sufficient: P2 expired EOA (7 d) and contract (24 h) sessions and P3 expired action confirmations refused; exempting either type from exp is killed. P1/P4 from Phase 2A.
changes.reason: new reproducible evidence (Phase 2B)

changes.why_sufficient: Challenge/session/action substitution and purpose swapping refused; accepting a challenge as session, any token as action, or ignoring the purpose is killed.
changes.remains_unproven: None beyond the HMAC boundary itself (CR-SESSION-001 P2/P3 stay open).
changes.reason: new reproducible evidence (Phase 2B)

changes.why_sufficient: P1 a session token in the login body is caught by the existing M1/Safe-App tests; P2 a Bearer fallback in the single session resolver is killed.

changes.reason: new reproducible evidence (Phase 2B)

changes.why_sufficient: P1 contract sessions without fresh authority killed; P2 legacy tokens without fresh authority and a getCode outage treated as "no code" killed; P3 not consuming the fresh confirmation killed by the replay assertion (409).
changes.remains_unproven: MUT-CR-AUTH-007-P2-NEW1 was dropped as an equivalent mutant: its catch branch is unreachable because perProvider() turns every provider error into {ok:false}; documented, not counted.
changes.reason: new reproducible evidence (Phase 2B)

changes.why_sufficient: Real Postgres: logout via the real handler writes the cutoff; every earlier session is refused at all five authenticated endpoint/method combinations; a later session works; the test kills a skipped server-side revoke, each endpoint ignoring revocation and an off-by-one boundary. Replaces the source-text-only evidence.
changes.remains_unproven: Production PostgREST/Supabase; attribution POST/DELETE share the GET session check and were not called separately.
changes.reason: new reproducible evidence (Phase 2B)

changes.why_sufficient: 2/10/25 truly concurrent revokes (barrier, zero timeouts) always store the maximum; a later lower request never lowers it; removing the max-merge or the advisory lock is killed.
changes.reason: new reproducible evidence (Phase 2B)
Phase 2A recorded SURVIVED (no test called /api/alerts without CRON_SECRET). test/cron-auth.test.mjs now kills it for the intended reason; declared KILLED.
catch { return false } in freshAuthorityRequired is unreachable: noContractCodeByQuorum never throws on provider failure. Replaced by MUT-CR-AUTH-007-P2-NEW3 on the reachable outage path.

P2 (stored expiry at the on-chain call site) is enforced twice (open check + atomic consume); removing one layer is equivalent at the security level and survives, so no single-property call-site mutation can prove it at E4. Not closed; the H2 primitive proof was not borrowed for a call-site property.
P2 constant-time comparison and P3 algorithm/key not selectable are not behaviourally observable with the current harness; left MISSING_EVIDENCE.
P1/P3 mutations that keep the signature check are equivalent (the session wallet is always the verified wallet); no honest E4 proof built in this batch.
allowed skip added for test/session-revocation-db.test.mjs :: REVOKE-DB, only while M1_DB_TEST_PG_URL is unset (same rule as M1/H2/L1/L5).
